title: Indicator times sign product factors over coordinates
statement:
Let $U, S \subseteq [n]$ with $S \subseteq U$, and let $\rho$ be a restriction on $n$ variables whose free-variable set is $J$. Write $\sigma(b) \in \{\pm1\}$ for the sign encoding of a bit $b$, and let $\ell(U,S,i,\rho(i))$ denote the per-coordinate local factor at coordinate $i$. Then
\[
  \mathbf{1}[\,U \cap J = S\,]\cdot \prod_{i \in U \setminus J} \sigma\bigl(\rho(i)\bigr)
  \;=\; \prod_{i=1}^{n} \ell\bigl(U, S, i, \rho(i)\bigr),
\]
where the left-hand side is read as $0$ whenever $U \cap J \neq S$. Equivalently, the product on the right vanishes unless the free coordinates of $\rho$ lying in $U$ are exactly $S$, in which case it equals the product of the $\pm1$-encodings of the bits that $\rho$ fixes on $U \setminus J$.
hypotheses_covered: S is a subset of U
ρ is a restriction on n variables
J is the free-variable set of ρ
left-hand side is 0 when U ∩ J ≠ S
replaced:
If $S \subseteq U$ then for every restriction $\rho$ with free set $J$,
\[
  \mathbf{1}[U \cap J = S]\cdot \mathrm{signProd}\,\rho\,(U \setminus J)
  \;=\; \prod_{i} \mathrm{localFactor}\,U\,S\,i\,(\rho\,i),
\]
where the left-hand side is understood as $0$ when the indicator fails.
